name: demo-lecture-v1
description: Ground-truth QA set authored against the SYNTHETIC demo fixture (data/fixtures/demo_lecture.json). Every gold span is a real interval of that transcript, so metrics computed from it are verifiable, not estimated. Includes 2 negatives: an unanswerable question and an off-topic question.

questions.question: Why are recurrent neural networks slow to train on GPUs?
questions.expected_answer: RNNs process one token at a time and each step depends on the previous hidden state, so computation cannot be parallelized across time, which is a disaster for GPU training speed.

questions.question: What problem do RNNs have with long-range dependencies?
questions.expected_answer: Information must travel through every intermediate hidden state, and gradients flow back along the same long path, so they vanish or explode; the path length grows linearly with distance.

questions.question: What is the core idea that makes self-attention better than recurrence?
questions.expected_answer: Every token looks directly at every other token in one step, so the path length between any two positions is constant (one operation) instead of growing with distance.

questions.question: What are queries, keys and values in self-attention?
questions.expected_answer: Each token produces three vectors: a query saying what it is looking for, a key saying what it contains, and a value carrying the information passed along when attended to.

questions.question: Why are attention dot products divided by the square root of the key dimension?
questions.expected_answer: Without scaling, large dimensions make dot products big, the softmax saturates, and gradients become tiny.

questions.question: How does masked self-attention work in the decoder?
questions.expected_answer: Scores of future positions are set to negative infinity before the softmax, so a token can never attend to later tokens, keeping autoregressive generation honest.

questions.question: How many attention heads does the original Transformer use and what are their dimensions?
questions.expected_answer: Eight attention heads, each with a dimension of sixty-four (64), for a total model dimension of five hundred twelve (512).

questions.question: Why does the Transformer need positional encodings?
questions.expected_answer: Self-attention is permutation invariant and has no built-in notion of order, so position information must be injected explicitly; the original paper adds sine and cosine functions of different frequencies to the embeddings.

questions.question: How does the computational complexity of self-attention compare with a recurrent layer?
questions.expected_answer: A recurrent layer costs n times d squared sequentially; self-attention costs n squared times d but fully in parallel; when n is smaller than d attention is cheaper and much faster on GPUs. The quadratic cost in n is attention's real weakness.

questions.question: What learning rate does the speaker recommend for fine-tuning BERT?
questions.expected_answer: About two times ten to the minus five (2e-5), up to five times ten to the minus five (5e-5) for fine-tuning a small Transformer like BERT base; for training from scratch use a larger learning rate around one times ten to the minus three (1e-3) with warmup.

questions.question: Why is learning-rate warmup essential when training Transformers?
questions.expected_answer: Early Adam second-moment estimates are unreliable, so large early updates destabilize training; the learning rate is increased linearly for the first few thousand steps (4000 in the original paper) and then decayed.

questions.question: What regularization does the Transformer use?
questions.expected_answer: Dropout of zero point one on attention weights and on sublayer outputs, plus label smoothing of zero point one during training; label smoothing hurts perplexity a little but improves accuracy and BLEU.

questions.question: Should you use pre-norm or post-norm, and why?
questions.expected_answer: Pre-norm (normalizing before each sublayer) is much more stable to train, especially without careful warmup.

questions.question: Which optimizer does the speaker recommend?
questions.expected_answer: Adam, or better AdamW with decoupled weight decay.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the video?
questions.expected_answer: The video explains the Transformer architecture from the ground up: why attention replaced recurrence, how self-attention works with queries keys and values, multi-head attention, positional encodings, and practical training tips.
